cases.name: clickable
cases.when: actionsEnabled is false or absent -- the chip root itself renders as <button>

cases.name: clickable-with-actions
cases.when: actionsEnabled is true -- a kebab cannot nest inside a button, so the root becomes a <div> and the interactive attributes move down to the chip BODY, a descendant <button>

reason: React declares a third case, `inert`, and derives it from whether `onClick` was passed. This layer cannot: Angular has no way to ask whether an output has subscribers -- OutputEmitterRef.listeners is private, and an `interactive` input would be a member no contract declares. It is the same wall TableRow's binding records, and this binding resolves it the OPPOSITE way on purpose. TableRow renders the non-interactive shape because always-a-button would put a dead tab stop on every row of every table; a chip is tabindex="-1" and is never a page tab stop, so always-a-button costs no dead stop here, where always-a-div would delete Enter-into-the-chip -- the whole keyboard story arena-calendar's `grid` binding leans on. `divergesFrom` names `none` because that is the pattern React's third case binds. The consequence is real and bounded: an Angular chip whose consumer bound no (click) is announced as a button that does nothing, and it is reachable only by Enter from the hour cell it overlaps, never by Tab.
